title: U.S. House · Texas's 31st Congressional District
area: Central Texas, primarily Williamson County (Round Rock, Georgetown) and part of Bell County (Killeen).

context.text: Texas redrew its congressional district boundaries in August 2025 ahead of the 2026 elections, a mid-decade redistricting.

In the March 3, 2026 primaries, incumbent John Carter won the Republican nomination with 59.7% of the vote in a ten-candidate field, and Justin Early defeated Stuart Whitlow 57.6% to 42.4% for the Democratic nomination. Greg Stoker advanced as the Green Party's nominee from its March 21, 2026 convention.

summary.text: John Carter is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 31st District, a lawyer and former Williamson County district judge first elected to Congress in 2002. He serves on the House Appropriations Committee and, according to his official website, chairs its Military Construction and Veterans Affairs subcommittee. He is seeking re-election in 2026.

background.text: Born in Houston, Texas; graduated from Bellaire High School.
Earned a B.A. from Texas Tech University in 1964 and a J.D. from the University of Texas in 1969.
Practiced law in Round Rock, Texas; according to his official website, he was one of two lawyers in the town when he settled in Central Texas.
Served as judge of the 277th District Court in Williamson County from 1981 to 2001; his official website says he was appointed to the bench and became known as "Judge."
Was first elected to Congress in 2002 and took office on January 3, 2003. His official website says he decided to run after the September 11, 2001 attacks.

Has served on the House Appropriations Committee, chairing its Homeland Security subcommittee from 2013 to 2016, serving as ranking member of the Military Construction and Veterans Affairs subcommittee in 2021-2022, and chairing that subcommittee in the 2025-2026 session. He also sits on the Defense and Commerce, Justice, Science subcommittees.
According to his official website, he has passed legislation under Presidents Bush, Obama and Trump, including the Veterans Transplant Coverage Act on VA coverage of live-donor transplants.
Describes himself as a Christian (Lutheran); according to his official website, he lives in Central Texas with his wife, Erika, and they have four children and eight grandchildren.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations and chairs its Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, and Related Agencies subcommittee in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Justin Early
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 57.6% of the vote

summary.text: Justin Early is the Democratic nominee, a U.S. Army veteran and cybersecurity architect from Georgetown who won the March 2026 Democratic primary with 57.6% of the vote. He has not held elected office. According to his campaign website, he is running on lower costs, higher wages, rules for artificial intelligence, and protecting Social Security and Medicare.

background.text: Describes himself as the eldest of three children of Wilson and Leisa Early, both U.S. Army veterans, in a working-class family; graduated from Leander High School in 1998.
Served in the U.S. Army from 1998 to 2006 as a paratrooper at Fort Bragg and later as a LAN systems administrator at the Defense Intelligence Agency in the Pentagon.
Has built a career in cybersecurity since leaving the military; currently a cybersecurity architect at Dell Technologies.
Has served as a Democratic precinct chair in Tarrant County, on a Human Relations Committee, and as a 2008 presidential delegate in Barack Obama's campaign.
Announced his candidacy for the 31st District in July 2025, according to the Williamson County Sun, and defeated Stuart Whitlow in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary, 57.6% to 42.4%.
According to his campaign, he lives in Georgetown, Texas, with his wife, Toni, and they have seven adult children.

priorities.text: His campaign website lists veterans' healthcare funding, clearing VA claims backlogs, and workplace protections such as paid family and sick leave among his priorities.

positions.summary: Says he would reverse VA funding cuts and clear claims and care backlogs so veterans are not made to wait for benefits.
Says he would work to shift the tax burden off working families, saying people should not pay a higher share than the wealthiest.

candidates.name: Greg Stoker
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced as the Green Party's nominee from its March 21, 2026 state convention

summary.text: Greg Stoker is the Green Party nominee, a former U.S. Army Ranger and podcast host who describes himself as an anti-war activist. He announced his campaign on January 15, 2026, and was placed on the ballot by the party's March 21, 2026 convention. He has not held elected office.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Army as a Ranger and was deployed to Afghanistan four times, according to Middle East Eye.

Became known as an anti-war commentator and podcast host on social media, and joined the Global Sumud Flotilla to Gaza in late September 2025, where he was arrested when Israeli forces boarded the vessels, according to Middle East Eye.

Announced his bid for Texas's 31st District in an Instagram video on January 15, 2026, saying he would not accept money from political action committees or corporate donors; advanced as the Green Party nominee at its March 21, 2026 convention.

researchNotes: Carter's positions are limited to official committee assignments; no 2026 Candidate Connection survey was found for him. No Candidate Connection survey or official campaign website was found for Greg Stoker, and his Ballotpedia page has no biography; his biography relies on one news report and may be incomplete. Federal key votes and FEC totals for the incumbent are added separately by script. Biography details for Justin Early come mainly from his Ballotpedia survey and campaign website and are self-described.
